title: EconWebArena: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents on Economic Tasks in Realistic Web Environments

event.name: Proceedings of the Fifth Workshop on Generation, Evaluation and Metrics (GEM)

container-title: Proceedings of the Fifth Workshop on Generation, Evaluation and Metrics (GEM)

items.abstract: <jats:p>The deployment of autonomous agents in safety-critical environments demands robust performance not only under expected conditions but also when confronted with rare, worstcase scenarios. Traditional evaluation pipelines, which rely on fixed test suites or stochastic environment sampling, often fail to expose latent vulnerabilities because they lack the capacity to systematically generate both realistic and challenging edge cases. In this work, we introduce a novel stress-testing framework based on adversarial self-play, wherein two competing agents-a protagonist and an adversary-are co-evolved in a shared environment. The adversary is trained to induce failures in the protagonist by discovering and exploiting its policy weaknesses, while the protagonist simultaneously adapts to improve its resilience. Crucially, we incorporate a realism constraint into the adversary's objective, regularizing its generated scenarios to remain within the bounds of physically plausible and semantically meaningful world dynamics. Through extensive experiments in continuous control and multi-agent navigation domains, we demonstrate that our approach produces a significantly higher density of failure-inducing states than random sampling or prior adversarial methods, while preserving scenario plausibility. Moreover, we show that agents trained against our adversarial self-play regime exhibit markedly improved robustness when deployed on unseen test distributions, without sacrificing nominal performance. Our framework offers a principled path toward automated, adaptive, and realistic stress-testing, bridging the gap between laboratory evaluation and real-world deployment demands.</jats:p>
